sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
Head: vertex and cheeks pale yellowish brown with a few short, stiff setae; frons yellowish brown, becoming dirty brown anteriorly, its anterior margin bearing a row of evenly spaced stiff setae, with a broad brown-black ridge extending from the anterior dorsal margin of the antennal socket toward the midline. Clypeus white, its margin translucent. Labrum large, brown, strongly convex, with a few yellow stiff setae. Compound eyes large, black, less than one eye-width from the lower margin of the head and about 1/4 eye-width from the antennal socket. Ocelli almost touching the compound eyes, their diameter about half the eye length. Scape, pedicel and flagellum pale yellowish brown; flagellum 14—16-segmented (about 2.7 mm long), about 2.1 times the length of the head capsule; basal flagellomere slightly longer than the remaining ones, dark yellowish brown. Thorax: dorsum pale yellowish brown, pleural region white. Pronotum 1.6 times as wide as long, both anterior and posterior margins shallowly concave. Tibial spurs 3:3:3, arolia absent. Wing membrane transparent, costa pale brown. Abdomen: dorsum pale yellowish brown, venter white with a pale yellow tinge.

Measurements (N=27, mm, mean±standard deviation (range)): head length to mandible base 1.29±0.06 (1.17—1.39); head width 1.23±0.03 (1.15—1.30); compound eye diameter 0.33±0.02 (0.29—0.37); distance from compound eye to lower margin of head 0.25±0.03 (0.19—0.33); ocellus length 0.17±0.02 (0.13—0.19); right basal flagellomere length 0.16±0.02 (0.13—0.23), width 0.11±0.01 (0.10—0.12); maximum pronotum length 0.89±0.05 (0.81—1.00), width 1.45±0.06 (1.31—1.58); body length with wings 14.93±1.17 (13.20—18.84). Also: body length without wings 7.61±0.79 (6.08—9.12); fore wing length from the shoulder suture 11.94±0.83 (10.64—14.88); fore wing width 3.63±0.23 (3.28—4.16).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Head: vertex and cheeks pale reddish brown with a few short, stiff setae; frons pale reddish brown, becoming dark brown anteriorly, its anterior margin with several long setae. The dorsal margin of the antennal socket forms a projecting blackish brown ridge, and a broad blackish brown ridge extends from the anterior dorsal margin toward the midline. Clypeus white. Labrum brown, 1.5 times as wide as long, with several short setae and 3—4 long setae at the apex of its dorsal surface. Mandible base dark reddish brown, becoming black anteriorly. Compound eyes small, oval, translucent, about 1.5 eye-widths from the antennal socket. Pedicel and scape blackish brown. Basal flagellomere 2.17 times as long as wide, equal in length to the following 3 segments together, dark reddish brown at the base, becoming brown toward the apical 1/4, the apical 1/3 inflated and bearing numerous brown long setae. Flagellum 10—12-segmented (12 in the holotype), extending 2—3 segments beyond the apex of the mandibles. Thorax: pronotum dark reddish brown, the dorsum and pleural region tinged with pale reddish brown; pronotum as wide as the head, its anterior margin concave and upturned, the lateral margins smoothly curved. Abdomen: dorsum and venter dirty pale reddish brown.

Measurements (N=84, mm, mean±standard deviation (range), holotype): head length to mandible base 2.38±0.16 (1.92—2.81), holotype 2.29; head width 1.74±0.09 (1.50—1.92), holotype 1.71; left mandible length 1.53±0.10 (1.27—1.73), holotype 1.50; postmentum maximum width 0.63±0.04 (0.56—0.75), holotype 0.58; postmentum minimum width 0.35±0.04 (0.27—0.46), holotype 0.37; postmentum length 1.47±0.17 (1.23—1.88), holotype 1.44; right basal flagellomere length 0.36±0.03 (0.28—0.44), width 0.16±0.01 (0.14—0.19); maximum pronotum length 1.18±0.10 (0.92—1.56), width 1.72±0.10 (1.46—1.92); head length/width 1.37±0.10 (1.10—1.59), holotype 1.34; pronotum length/width 0.69±0.05 (0.59—0.77), holotype 0.71.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Holotype soldier: 1.1 miles north of Aguanga, California, 116°52′W 33°27′N, elevation 658 m (2160 ft), 3 January 1978 (month 1), collected by M. K. Rust and R. H. Scheffrahn from jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis). Paratype soldiers (all from jojoba unless stated otherwise): 16 from the same colony, 3 and 7 more from the same locality on the same day; 5.6 miles south of Sage, Riverside County, California (116°54′W 33°31′N, 701 m), 2, 3 and 2 individuals (28 April 1977 (month 4), 10 May (month 5), 5 May (month 5)), 2 individuals on 16 December 1977 (month 12) (collected by C. Barbour and R. E. Wagner); 2, 4, 5, 7 and 15 individuals from different colonies collected from sugarbush (Rhus ovata) on 19 February 1978 (month 2). Paratype alates: 5.6 miles south of Sage, 21 individuals on 30 June 1977 (month 6) (collected by M. K. Rust and D. A. Reierson); the colony collected on 19 February 1978 (month 2) produced 6 individuals in the laboratory. The specific name is formed from frutex (shrub) and cavus (hollowed out), referring to its habit of boring into living shrubs.

note: Adapted from the original description (in English) published with the species by Rust (1979); both the alate and the soldier have prose descriptions by body region (head / thorax / abdomen) and measurement tables (N=27, N=84, mean±SD (range)). The species is named for its habit of boring into living jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis) shrubs.
